extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator (early 18th-century British literate public) interested in moral conduct, courtship, marriage, and domestic manners
extracted.subtask_description: A set of prescriptive essays and letters giving practical guidance on benevolence, courtship, marriage, needlework, and public behaviour for readers of The Spectator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire not more than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire not more of the World than is necessary to accommodate you in passing through it; look upon every thing beyond, not as useless only, but burthensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to learn the true estimate of things: keep desires limited to what is necessary so as to avoid additional burdens and discontent; contrasted with the competitive pursuit of wealth/power that creates rivals and unhappiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid goods that make enemies
rubrics_metrics.description: Place not your Quiet in Things, which you cannot have without putting others beside them, and thereby making them your Enemies; and which, when attain'd, will give you more Trouble to keep, than Satisfaction in the Enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek exclusive or scarce goods whose attainment requires displacing others; such acquisitions generate hostility and more trouble than pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue is communal and grows by sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is a Good of a nobler kind; it grows by Communication, and so little resembles earthly Riches, that the more Hands it is lodged in, the greater is every Man's particular Stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts virtue with wealth: whereas riches are diminished by division, virtue increases when shared. Encourage propagating and mingling benevolence as a way to increase individual happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wealth chiefly to do good
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wealth be an Instrument of Pleasure, the greatest Pleasure it can put into your Power, is that of doing Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wealth should be used instrumentally to promote beneficence; the pleasure from beneficence enlarges happiness beyond private sensual gratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate calm, contented mind for benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: The last Enemy to Benevolence I shall mention is Uneasiness of any Kind... A guilty, or a discontented Mind ... hath not Leisure to attend to the Necessity or Reasonableness of a Kindness desired, nor a Taste for those Pleasures which wait on Beneficence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid guilt, discontent, or fretting; a calm and unpolluted heart is required to relish the pleasures of giving and to be benevolent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the softest times to request favors
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a Favour to request of any one, to observe the softest times of Address, when the Soul, in a Flush of good Humour, takes a Pleasure to shew it self pleased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: ask for favors when the person is in good humour and disposed to generosity. Example: address people when they are relaxed and pleased to increase chance of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate integrity, self-satisfaction, and faith to foster goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons conscious of their own integrity, satisfied with themselves, and their Condition, and full of Confidence in a Supreme Being, and the Hope of Immortality, survey all about them with a Flow of Good-will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A composed mind, self-respect, and religious hope make one more benevolent and disposed to goodwill toward others; 'place the Mind in its right Posture' to reveal propensity to beneficence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appear important to attract attention
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Person so irresistable as one who is a Man of Importance, provided it be in Matters of no Consequence. One who makes himself talked of ... is in a fair way of being a Favourite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation, even for trivial distinctions or being talked about, increases social attractiveness. Examples: bowing to people, seeming acquainted with elites, making a name (even via cocky acts) aids courtship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notoriety and reputation for intrigue can attract lovers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a strange Curiosity in the female World to be acquainted with the dear Man who has been loved by others... His Reputation does more than half his Business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reputation as an intriguing rake or someone who has 'ruined the greatest Number of Reputations' can paradoxically draw interest; reputation for conquest arouses curiosity among some women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical courtship tactics: proximity, plausible talk, and confident affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the theatre: 'Close as you can to hers, and Side by Side... Then find Occasion to begin Discourse, Enquire whose Chariot this... Like what she likes... Call this Armenia, that, the Caspian Shore: Talk probably; no Matter for the Truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tactics for public flirtation: sit close, initiate conversation about the spectacle, mirror her tastes, speak plausibly (even invent knowledge) to appear charming and knowledgeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage can produce love ('If she marries first, Love will come after')
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not impossible but she may, in time, have a true Affection for him who is, at present, indifferent to her ... If she marries first, Love will come after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pragmatic counsel that marriage may develop genuine affection over time; choose long-term considerations (children, shared life) and allow custom to foster love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaisance and mutual teasing may signal underlying affection
rubrics_metrics.description: The only Objection ... is his want of Complaisance, which ... she is very willing to return. ... It is difficult to determine, whether Love delights more in giving Pleasure or Pain. ... Imitation is a kind of artless Flattery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal teasing, provocation, and the tendency to imitate a partner's expressions or mannerisms are signs of mutual interest; catching another's habits indicates fondness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage requires pursuit of common interest and united care for children
rubrics_metrics.description: I need not insist upon the Necessity of their pursuing one common Interest, and their united Care, for their Children; but shall only observe ... that married Persons are both more warm in their Love, and more hearty in their Hatred, than any others whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical expectation: spouses should work toward common goals, especially child-rearing, which both strengthens affection and intensifies mutual commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom and constant conversation foster mutual friendship
rubrics_metrics.description: The great Efficacy of Custom, and constant Conversation, to produce a mutual Friendship and Benevolence in two Persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular interaction, shared daily life, and habit produce closeness and affection; marriage's routine can lead to deeper friendship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouses tend to become like each other over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Let my fair Correspondent therefore consider, that the Gentleman recommended will have a good deal of her own Face in two or three Years; which she must not expect from the Beau, who is too full of his dear self to copy after another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe that couples often adopt each other's speech, manner, and even features over time; this is offered as a benefit of steady partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage needlework as moral and domestic duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend the long neglected Art of Needle-work ... Those Hours which in this Age are thrown away in Dress, Play, Visits, and the like, were employ'd in writing out Receipts, or working Beds, Chairs, and Hangings for the Family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Needlework is promoted as a virtuous pastime that exhibits genius, keeps women out of scandal, reduces unnecessary expense, and provides household profit and industry; it is suitable even for those without literary genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic arts over literary vanity: channel creative talent to tapestry
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Pastoral Poetesses may vent their Fancy in Rural Landskips, and place despairing Shepherds under silken Willows ... The Heroick Writers may work up Battles as successfully, and inflame them with Gold or stain them with Crimson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates applying literary or poetic imagination to domestic productions (tapestry, embroidery) as a more appropriate and profitable expression for women in society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rules to revive needlework (three household requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals: I. That no young Virgin whatsoever be allow'd to receive the Addresses of her first Lover, but in a Suit of her own Embroidering. II. That before every fresh Servant, she be oblig'd to appear with a new Stomacher at the least. III. That no one be actually married, till she hath the Child-bed Pillows, &c. ready Stitched, as likewise the Mantle for the Boy quite finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete household standards proposed as laws to encourage productive needlework and signal domestic preparedness prior to courtship and marriage; presented as practical requirements that would restore industry and thrift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needlework reduces scandal and idle political talk
rubrics_metrics.description: Another Argument for busying good Women in Works of Fancy, is, because it takes them off from Scandal, the usual Attendant of Tea-Tables, and all other unactive Scenes of Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement in craftwork is recommended as a social remedy: occupied hands reduce gossip, factional disputes (Whig/Tory), and excessive talk at tea-tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion as an essential quality for spouses
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretion seems absolutely necessary, and accordingly we find that the best Husbands have been most famous for their Wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wisdom and prudent judgement are required in marital partners; discretion helps sustain the duties and steadiness of married life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue yields constancy and mutual esteem in marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is the next necessary Qualification for this domestick Character, as it naturally produces Constancy and mutual Esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral character and virtue are foundational to stable marriage; they produce fidelity and reciprocal respect, illustrated by classical examples (Brutus and Porcia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-nature and evenness of temper required
rubrics_metrics.description: Good-Nature is a third necessary Ingredient in the Marriage-State... Good-Nature is insufficient, unless it be steady and uniform, and accompanied with an Evenness of Temper, which is, above all things, to be preserved in this Friendship contracted for Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A constant, even temper and good-nature are emphasized as vital to maintain harmonious married life and to manage the inevitable strains of domesticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bear with each other's faults during the first year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the wedded Pair would but habituate themselves for the first Year to bear with one another's Faults, the Difficulty would be pretty well conquer'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical recommendation: tolerate early imperfections and cultivate patience during the first year of marriage to establish stability and mutual habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should expect criticism and hostility
rubrics_metrics.description: While I was employing my self for the Good of Mankind, I was surpriz'd to meet with very unsuitable Returns from my Fellow-Creatures. Never was poor Author so beset with Pamphleteers ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for public writers: anticipate pamphleteers, lampoons, and sudden attacks from diverse quarters (including people of varying ranks); cultivate a small circle of supportive friends and persist in work despite detractors.
